rawFindings.title: Literal-only concatenations are now reported as template candidates
rawFindings.explanation: The new fallback treats any non-`Literal` AST node as a non-literal value. That makes semantically literal operands such as unary numeric literals and no-substitution template literals count as dynamic, so the rule reports concatenations that contain no variable/expression interpolation and were previously considered valid literal-only concatenations.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore literal-like handling in `hasNonLiteral`, e.g. recurse into `UnaryExpression` operands and treat template literals with no expressions as literals before falling back to `node.type !== "Literal"`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With `prefer-template` enabled, `var foo = +100 + 'yen';` now reports `Unexpected string concatenation.` even though all operands are constant literals; likewise ``var foo = `foo` + "bar";`` reports despite being literal-only.
